subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm: stop calling pmd_folio() on special PMDs

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested a more efficient approach to handle special PMDs by using vm_normal_folio_pmd() and minimizing checks on the expected path, specifically for huge zero pmds.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) suggested dropping the is_huge_zero_pmd() check, as !vm_normal_folio_pmd() already includes the huge zero folio.
reviews.raw_body:
I think you can now drop the is_huge_zero_pmd() check, because
!vm_normal_folio_pmd() includes the huge zero folio.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledged that the patch conflicts with zone device fixes and is unsure of the best approach to resolve this, but did not provide a plan for addressing it.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledges that David's feedback about removing existing checks was correct and agrees to take another look at the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
I was err'ing on the side of not removing existing checks, but I can
take a look.  Trivilially - I think you are right.

~Gregory

2026-08-27.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where special page table walkers (pmd_folio()) are called on PMDs that do not map refcounted struct pages, leading to faults when accessing folio fields. The patches modify the pmd_folio() calls in two walkers and introduce a new function vm_normal_folio() for PMD halves, matching the existing PTE halves. This change affects four callers of vmf_insert_pfn_pmd(), which installs special PMDs holding raw pfn mappings without memmap entries. As a result, mbind(MPOL_MF_STRICT) over PMD mapped VM_PFNMAP regions now returns 0 instead of -EIO.
